speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are experiencing dizziness, nausea, and imbalance. To begin our evaluation, can you tell me if these symptoms started suddenly or developed gradually?

speaker: Patient
text: 27-year-old male. The patient reports a sustained sensation of the room spinning since this morning, which is low grade and constant. He occasionally feels nauseous and has taken diphenhydramine to help him sleep, which also alleviates his symptoms slightly. He mentions recent increased intake of garlic due to trying to recover from a cold a few days ago. Past medical history is unremarkable.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo (BPPV) - The patient reports a sudden onset of constant room spinning (vertigo) with nausea and relief from diphenhydramine, consistent with acute vestibular dysfunction. While the garlic intake is noted, it is unlikely to be the primary cause of sustained rotational vertigo. To confirm the diagnosis and rule out other causes, I need to perform a physical exam. Are you willing for me to check your eyes for nystagmus and move your head in specific ways?
